items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: I know Squibb once said, they have orders for about four hundred from libraries.

ctx.x: Well, I don't know whether they could have been charged. They might have been charged. There was no, the first royalty was all used up anyway with the free copies that we had to give away. See, books like this, everybody wants copies of it. That's one reason I figured the Jelly Roll book, I'd better wait a few years until everybody's dead. I've promised so many copies. I've had over sixty interviews, and there are about a dozen people who wrote articles, some of them reprints like Charles Smith and Danny Barker…
You could go to Preservation Hall and sell a thousand a night. Just sign your name on them. I know Squibb once said, they have orders for about four hundred from libraries.

It's about the main sale that they get. And all of us jazz fans would be too poor to buy a twenty dollar book anyway, hard and early. I got the Eddie Condon book the other day. How much did you have to pay for that book? It paid seven dollars or something. That's good. I paid seventeen fifty. Yeah seventeen fifty. So I never would have bought that if it, except it was less than half price. Did I ever tell you what Pickle Jackson told me?
